section_summary: Pages 161–186 finish a June 1938 report on Japanese shipping, covering whaling rules, shipping agreements and services, company finances, salvage, freight rates, fishing disputes, shipbuilding, and naval vessels. Later pages contain a State Department instruction about ship scrapping, a file note and shipping excerpt concerning Japan–China routes, and an internal memorandum requesting Maritime Commission material.

subfiles.title: Shipping in the Japanese Empire during June 1938
subfiles.about: The concluding pages survey developments in Japanese fisheries and merchant shipping during June 1938.
subfiles.summary: The report discusses fishery cooperatives, Japan’s participation in whaling negotiations, a renewed Japan–Australia shipping agreement, and a dispute within the Philippine–New York freight conference. It records route changes, company mergers and dividends, iron salvage, charter and freight rates, coal supplies, and a Soviet–Japanese fishing permit dispute. It also describes a floating prison, the end of a Sydney dockworkers’ boycott, and tables of ships under construction and merchant tonnage, followed by sources.

subfiles.title: Naval Construction
subfiles.about: Reports the launch of the Japanese repair ship Akashi and delivery of vessels built for Siam.
subfiles.summary: The report gives specifications and construction details for the Japanese Navy’s new repair ship Akashi, launched at Sasebo on June 29. It also describes the departure of four submarines with trained Siamese crews and delivery of a Siamese gunboat built at Kobe.

subfiles.title: Instruction concerning ship scrapping information
subfiles.about: Requests continued reporting on ship scrapping and acknowledges a July 1938 shipping report.
subfiles.summary: Requests ship scrapping updates; rates Affeld’s shipping report “very good” and asks that he be informed.

subfiles.title: Unidentified filing notation
subfiles.about: Contains only fragmentary handwritten or stamped filing marks and dates.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary filing marks; no substantive text is legible.

subfiles.title: Document file note on Japanese shipping
subfiles.about: Cross-references a report on vessel subsidies and shipping between Japan, China, North Korea, and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: Indexes a report on vessel subsidies, China routes, Yangtze plans, and shipping consolidation.

subfiles.title: Shipping
subfiles.about: Describes proposed merchant-vessel construction subsidies and expanded Japanese shipping in China.
subfiles.summary: The Communications Office reportedly planned subsidies for small and medium merchant vessels. Nippon Yusen would add liners to the Kobe–Shanghai route; Shozo Murata described plans to expand Nisshin Steamship’s Yangtze service. A new company was reported to be consolidating shipping interests between Japan, North Korea, and Manchukuo.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Maritime Commission releases
subfiles.about: Requests distribution of Maritime Commission releases to consulates and future reporting on the subject.
subfiles.summary: Asks that Kobe and Yokohama consulates receive December Maritime Commission releases and report related material.
